## isocast

```text
Isocast: scene-based recording with per-source ISO files, controlled from the command line or by agents

Usage: isocast <COMMAND>

Commands:
  report-file  Read a bounded page from a redacted report preview
  report       Create a private, redacted bug-report zip. Nothing is uploaded unless you pass --submit
  logs         Read structured logs (also works when the daemon is stopped)
  hotkeys      Customize profile hotkeys, including global keys and push-to-talk
  encoders     List recording codecs and the containers each supports
  setup        Work with setup files
  collection   Scene collections, as in OBS: named sets of scenes, sources, transitions and the canvas size, swapped as a whole. The one in use is the live setup's (with the profile in use)
  profile      Profiles, as in OBS: named frame rate, recording, stream and audio settings, swapped as a whole. The one in use is the live setup's (with the scene collection in use)
  plugin       Plugins: folders with an isocast-plugin.toml, installed from a local folder. A plugin's process runs sandboxed and may only call the methods it was granted
  data         The data store: values by key (like `score.home`) that text in scenes shows (`data = "score.home"` on a text source or text content), set by you, scripts, agents and plugins without changing the setup
  timeline     Timelines: takes in order, joined into one file by `export`. While one is current, every take that finishes (`stop`, or a `split`) is added to its end; `retake` records the last one again
  project      Recording projects: a folder per recording session (`<date> <time> Untitled` in the recordings folder) with every take's files, manifests and exports
  retake       Record the last take again. Not recording (or while a stop is finishing, once it has): take the current timeline's last clip off (its files stay) and start recording. Recording: drop the take being recorded from the timeline (its files stay) and begin a new take about a quarter second later, without stopping any device; returns once it has begun
  devices      List displays, windows, cameras, microphones and audio outputs (for monitoring), with their ids and formats, and the permissions recording them needs
  record       Record a setup's ISO sources, each to its own file, until --seconds runs out or Ctrl-C. Without a setup file, record --source specs
  start        Start recording in the background (in isocastd, launched if needed) and return once every file is created. Same options as `record`; with neither a setup nor --source, records the live setup. A setup or --source given here becomes the live setup
  stop         Stop the background recording and print its report
  pause        Pause this take without closing its files; streaming continues
  resume       Resume the paused take into the same files
  status       Show whether isocastd is recording, with live counters
  split        Split the background recording into a new take at the next whole second, without stopping any device
  marker       Mark this moment in the background recording, with a label
  refresh      Reload a browser source's page in the background recording, bypassing the cache
  scene        Put a scene on air, by id, with its transition (the scene's, else the setup's) unless --cut, --fade MS or --transition is given. While recording, the switch goes into the manifest's scene timeline
  preview      Stage a scene in preview, by id, to put on air with `take`
  take         Put the preview scene on air (with its transition unless --cut, --fade MS or --transition is given); the scene that was on air moves to preview
  doctor       Check this Mac and a setup: permissions, hardware encoders, whether the setup's devices are connected, and the recording disk's space and speed. Exits with an error if anything would stop a recording
  tune         Benchmark the encoders on a setup's files (the live setup if none is given), all at once as in a recording, and say whether this Mac keeps up (fits, keeps up with no margin, or can't keep up). If it doesn't fit, try changes closest first (a smaller program file, a lower quality preset, half the frame rate, one ISO file fewer) and recommend the closest that fits, as a patch for `plan` and `apply`. `start` warns when a setup exceeds what this measured. Runs in isocastd
  capacity     Predict, instantly and without benchmarking, whether a setup's files (the live setup's, at its sources' live formats, if none is given) fit this Mac's video encoders, from measured per-chip data, and list the closest changes that fit as patches for `plan` and `apply`. `tune` measures instead. Runs in isocastd
  optimize     Optimize the live setup for recording, streaming or both, like OBS's Auto-Configuration Wizard: recording favours quality and ISO files; streaming sets the service and a bitrate from the upload speed (tested unless --upload-kbps is given; a custom server only with `isocast stream speed-test`). Then `tune` benchmarks this Mac and steps down where it can't keep up. Prints a one-line summary and the changes; --apply makes them. Runs in isocastd
  snapshot     Save one frame as a PNG: of a video source (an id of the live setup, or a quick source like `screen` or `camera:NAME`), of --scene ID, of --preview, or with none of them the program (while recording, the exact frame it recorded last). Runs in isocastd
  audio        Change an audio source's program mix in the live setup: gain in dB, mute, sync offset in ms (positive is later), balance (-1 left to 1 right) and monitoring (hearing it through `audio.monitoring_device`). A running recording follows all but the offset at once
  restart      Restart isocastd, for example after granting it screen recording permission. Refused, atomically by isocastd, while it records, streams, exports or feeds the virtual camera
  permissions  Show the screen recording, camera and microphone permissions and what to do about each that isn't granted; with --request, ask macOS for the ones not decided yet (its prompts appear; --request camera asks for that one only) and wait up to a minute for the answers; with --open, open the System Settings pane where one is turned on
  get          Print the live setup (TOML, or JSON with --json) and its revision; with --resolved, also where layout put every item (each item's rect in its parent and its box on the canvas)
  plan         Show what a change to the live setup would do, without doing it: a whole setup FILE, or --patch with a JSON merge patch (lists of sources, scenes and items merge by id)
  apply        Make a change to the live setup, if it is still at --revision (from `plan` or `get`; 0 when there is no live setup yet)
  stream       Stream the program live over RTMP or RTMPS to the live setup's [stream] service, and keep its stream key in the Keychain
  replay       The replay buffer: keep the last seconds of the program in memory, and save them to a file on demand
  vcam         Feed a picture to Isocast Virtual Camera (extension approval required once)
  debug        Developer mode, for testing a build locally: verbose logs of every API call and component, and frame timing traces while recording
  watch        Print events from isocastd as they happen, until Ctrl-C
  frame        Save the live engine's newest frame of the program (the default), studio mode's preview, or a video source as a JPEG. Starts the engine if it isn't running
  frames       Record what a monitor shows: the live engine's low-latency H.264 stream of the program (the default), studio mode's preview or a video source, saved as an H.264 elementary stream (Annex B, which ffprobe and ffplay read). Starts the engine if it isn't running
  engine       Keep the live engine running (`start`), or let it stop once nothing needs it (`stop`). It runs the live setup's sources, program and mix all the time, so recording starts at once; it also runs while recording or while a client shows frames
  mcp          Serve the control API to agents over MCP, on stdin and stdout
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Getting started: `isocast permissions` shows what macOS allows, `isocast setup init --apply` makes a setup from this Mac's devices, `isocast frame` saves a picture of the program, `isocast start --seconds 10` records a test, and `isocast status` shows how it went. Agents: `isocast mcp`.
```

## isocast report-file

```text
Read a bounded page from a redacted report preview

Usage: isocast report-file [OPTIONS] <PREVIEW_ID> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <PREVIEW_ID>  
  <FILE>        

Options:
      --offset <OFFSET>  [default: 0]
      --limit <LIMIT>    
      --json             
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## isocast report

```text
Create a private, redacted bug-report zip. Nothing is uploaded unless you pass --submit

Usage: isocast report [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --out <OUT>                
      --describe <DESCRIBE>      
      --preview                  
      --private                  Pseudonymize paths, titles, device names and device IDs per report [alias: --hash-paths]
      --launches <LAUNCHES>      
      --submit                   Also send it: ISSUE.md becomes a public GitHub issue, and the zip is kept privately for the maintainers. Prints the issue URL
      --preview-id <PREVIEW_ID>  With --submit: send exactly this preview (from --preview)
      --json                     
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

```text
Usage: isocast logs [OPTIONS]

      --follow                 
      --level <LEVEL>          
      --component <COMPONENT>  
      --json                   
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

## isocast hotkeys

```text
Customize profile hotkeys, including global keys and push-to-talk

Usage: isocast hotkeys <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list      Current profile bindings and native registration warnings
  set       Bind an id to a chord and action (replace that binding only)
  unset     Remove a binding by id
  actions   Stable action catalogue, schemas, key names and suggested defaults
  defaults  Add defaults without replacing custom ids or occupied chords
  input     Forward focused fallback input. A one-shot press pulses; --hold-ms keeps the connection open and sends a release after the hold
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast setup

```text
Work with setup files

Usage: isocast setup <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check         Validate a setup file (.toml or .json) and summarize it
  schema        Print the JSON Schema of the setup document
  init          Make a good starting setup from this Mac's devices: the main display, the best camera and the default microphone, with desktop audio, in scenes "Screen + Camera", "Camera" and "Screen", recording the program and ISO files of the screen and camera (in isocastd). Prints it as TOML, writes it to --output, or makes it the live setup with --apply
  discover-obs  Find OBS Studio's scene collections and profiles on this Mac (in ~/Library/Application Support/obs-studio, or --folder), without importing anything: each collection with the profile an import would use, and each profile's video, recording and stream settings
  import-obs    Import an OBS Studio scene collection as a setup: its sources, scenes and items, filters and transition, matched against this Mac's devices (in isocastd). Prints the setup as TOML, or writes it to --output, and lists what couldn't come over
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast setup init

```text
Make a good starting setup from this Mac's devices: the main display, the best camera and the default microphone, with desktop audio, in scenes "Screen + Camera", "Camera" and "Screen", recording the program and ISO files of the screen and camera (in isocastd). Prints it as TOML, writes it to --output, or makes it the live setup with --apply

Usage: isocast setup init [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>          Write the setup to this file (it must not exist yet)
      --apply                    Make it the live setup, replacing any (kept in the setup file's .bak)
      --display <DISPLAY>        The display: "main" (the default), or an id or name from `isocast devices`
      --camera <CAMERA>          The camera: an id or (part of a) name from `isocast devices`, or "none". The best real camera if absent
      --microphone <MICROPHONE>  The microphone: "default" (the default), an id or (part of a) name, or "none"
      --no-system-audio          Leave desktop (system) audio out of the program
      --layout <LAYOUT>          Where the camera goes in "Screen + Camera": bottom_right (the default), bottom_left, top_right, top_left or side_by_side. A tall canvas stacks the screen and the camera
      --canvas <WxH[@FPS]>       The canvas, WIDTHxHEIGHT or WIDTHxHEIGHT@FPS; 1920x1080@60 by default
      --folder <FOLDER>          Recording folder; ~/Movies/Isocast by default
      --name <NAME>              The setup's name
      --json                     Print the result (setup, notes, applied change) as JSON
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

## isocast setup discover-obs

```text
Find OBS Studio's scene collections and profiles on this Mac (in ~/Library/Application Support/obs-studio, or --folder), without importing anything: each collection with the profile an import would use, and each profile's video, recording and stream settings

Usage: isocast setup discover-obs [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --folder <FOLDER>  Look in this folder instead
      --json             
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## isocast setup import-obs

```text
Import an OBS Studio scene collection as a setup: its sources, scenes and items, filters and transition, matched against this Mac's devices (in isocastd). Prints the setup as TOML, or writes it to --output, and lists what couldn't come over

Usage: isocast setup import-obs [OPTIONS] <COLLECTION>

Arguments:
  <COLLECTION>  A collection's .json file, or its name in OBS's scenes folder (like "Recording")

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>     Write the setup to this file (it must not exist yet)
      --canvas <WxH[@FPS]>  Import onto this canvas, WIDTHxHEIGHT or WIDTHxHEIGHT@FPS, scaling positions and sizes; the collection's own canvas and the profile's frame rate otherwise
      --profile <PROFILE>   The OBS profile with the frame rate and recording settings: a name or a basic.ini path. Found automatically if absent
      --json                Print the result (setup, what wasn't imported, notes) as JSON
  -h, --help                Print help
```

## isocast collection

```text
Scene collections, as in OBS: named sets of scenes, sources, transitions and the canvas size, swapped as a whole. The one in use is the live setup's (with the profile in use)

Usage: isocast collection <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list       List them, marking the one in use
  new        Make a new one: a scene collection with one empty scene on the canvas in use, or a profile with starter settings (60 fps, HEVC program and ISO files to ~/Movies/Isocast)
  duplicate  Copy one (by id) under a new name
  rename     Rename one (its id stays)
  delete     Delete one that isn't in use; its file is kept in the library's `deleted` folder
  switch     Use it: the live setup becomes it at once, and the live engine follows (a collection restores its last program/preview selection). Refused while recording or streaming
  import     Add one from a file: one exported with `export` (.toml or .json), or a whole setup file, which adds its collection and its profile. With --obs, from OBS Studio instead: a scene collection (its name or .json file) or a profile (its name, folder or basic.ini)
  export     Write one (the one in use if no id is given) to a file, .toml or .json, or print it as TOML; `import` adds it back, here or on another Mac
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast collection list

```text
List them, marking the one in use

Usage: isocast collection list [OPTIONS]
```

```text
      --json  
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast collection switch

```text
Use it: the live setup becomes it at once, and the live engine follows (a collection restores its last program/preview selection). Refused while recording or streaming

Usage: isocast collection switch [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  

Options:
      --with <ID>  Also switch the other half at the same time: the profile (for a collection) or the collection (for a profile), by id
      --json       
  -h, --help       Print help
```

## isocast collection import

```text
Add one from a file: one exported with `export` (.toml or .json), or a whole setup file, which adds its collection and its profile. With --obs, from OBS Studio instead: a scene collection (its name or .json file) or a profile (its name, folder or basic.ini)

Usage: isocast collection import [OPTIONS] [FILE]

Arguments:
  [FILE]  

Options:
      --obs <NAME_OR_FILE>          
      --obs-profile <NAME_OR_FILE>  For a scene collection from OBS: also import this OBS profile (name, folder or basic.ini), with Source Record's ISO settings
      --name <NAME>                 The name to give it; its own if absent
      --canvas <WxH>                For a scene collection from OBS: import it onto this canvas, WIDTHxHEIGHT, scaling positions and sizes
      --switch                      Switch to what was imported
      --obs-stream-key              Move the stream key OBS keeps in plain text in the OBS profile's service.json into the Keychain
      --json                        
  -h, --help                        Print help
```

## isocast collection export

```text
Write one (the one in use if no id is given) to a file, .toml or .json, or print it as TOML; `import` adds it back, here or on another Mac

Usage: isocast collection export [OPTIONS] [ID]

Arguments:
```

## isocast profile

```text
Profiles, as in OBS: named frame rate, recording, stream and audio settings, swapped as a whole. The one in use is the live setup's (with the scene collection in use)

Usage: isocast profile <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list       List them, marking the one in use
  new        Make a new one: a scene collection with one empty scene on the canvas in use, or a profile with starter settings (60 fps, HEVC program and ISO files to ~/Movies/Isocast)
  duplicate  Copy one (by id) under a new name
  rename     Rename one (its id stays)
  delete     Delete one that isn't in use; its file is kept in the library's `deleted` folder
  switch     Use it: the live setup becomes it at once, and the live engine follows (a collection restores its last program/preview selection). Refused while recording or streaming
  import     Add one from a file: one exported with `export` (.toml or .json), or a whole setup file, which adds its collection and its profile. With --obs, from OBS Studio instead: a scene collection (its name or .json file) or a profile (its name, folder or basic.ini)
  export     Write one (the one in use if no id is given) to a file, .toml or .json, or print it as TOML; `import` adds it back, here or on another Mac
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast plugin

```text
Plugins: folders with an isocast-plugin.toml, installed from a local folder. A plugin's process runs sandboxed and may only call the methods it was granted

Usage: isocast plugin <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add      Install a plugin from its folder (one with an isocast-plugin.toml): the folder is copied into the plugins folder and its process, if it has one, starts at once. Without --allow it only lists the permissions the plugin asks for
  list     List the installed plugins: version, what they provide, state, process and what they were granted
  remove   Stop a plugin's process and remove it (its data folder is kept if it wrote anything there). Refused while the live setup uses its kinds, unless --force
  enable   Turn a plugin on again (also after it crashed too often)
  disable  Turn a plugin off: its process stops until it is enabled
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast plugin add

```text
Install a plugin from its folder (one with an isocast-plugin.toml): the folder is copied into the plugins folder and its process, if it has one, starts at once. Without --allow it only lists the permissions the plugin asks for

Usage: isocast plugin add [OPTIONS] <PATH>

Arguments:
  <PATH>  

Options:
      --allow  Grant the permissions it asks for (they are printed without this)
      --link   Link to the folder instead of copying it, for developing a plugin: it is read again each time the plugin starts
      --force  Install it even if the same or a newer version is installed
      --json   
  -h, --help   Print help
```

## isocast plugin list

```text
List the installed plugins: version, what they provide, state, process and what they were granted

Usage: isocast plugin list [OPTIONS]

  -h, --help  Print help
```

```text
      --force  Remove it even though the live setup uses its kinds: they stay in the setup, bypassed, until the plugin is added again
```

## isocast data

```text
The data store: values by key (like `score.home`) that text in scenes shows (`data = "score.home"` on a text source or text content), set by you, scripts, agents and plugins without changing the setup

Usage: isocast data <COMMAND>

Commands:
  get     Show data keys and their values: every key, the KEYs given, or those under --prefix
  set     Set KEY to VALUE: JSON (`'"Hello"'`, `3`, `'{"home": 2}'`), or else the text as it is (`Hello`). Text showing the key (`data = "KEY"`) changes at once. Keys are dotted ids like `score.home`

  -h, --help  Print help
```


```text
Set KEY to VALUE: JSON (`'"Hello"'`, `3`, `'{"home": 2}'`), or else the text as it is (`Hello`). Text showing the key (`data = "KEY"`) changes at once. Keys are dotted ids like `score.home`
```


## isocast timeline

```text
Timelines: takes in order, joined into one file by `export`. While one is current, every take that finishes (`stop`, or a `split`) is added to its end; `retake` records the last one again

Usage: isocast timeline <COMMAND>

Commands:
  new     Make a timeline and make it current: from now on every take that finishes (`stop`, or a `split`) is added to its end
  list    List the timelines, and which is current
  open    Make a timeline current (by id), so finished takes are added to it
  close   Make no timeline current: takes are only recorded
  show    Show a timeline (the current one unless an id is given): its clips in order, each with its take and files, and the takes taken off it
  remove  Take a clip off the timeline (by id, like c2). Its take's files stay where they are
  move    Move a clip (by id) to POSITION, counting from 1 (the first)
  export  Join the clips, in order, into one program file and one file per ISO source every clip has (the video as recorded, no re-encoding), plus an .export.json manifest; waits for it unless --background
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```


## isocast retake

```text
Record the last take again. Not recording (or while a stop is finishing, once it has): take the current timeline's last clip off (its files stay) and start recording. Recording: drop the take being recorded from the timeline (its files stay) and begin a new take about a quarter second later, without stopping any device; returns once it has begun

Usage: isocast retake [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --folder <FOLDER>    Write the new take here; else where the take it replaces is
      --seconds <SECONDS>  Stop on its own after this many seconds
      --json               
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## isocast tune

```text
Benchmark the encoders on a setup's files (the live setup if none is given), all at once as in a recording, and say whether this Mac keeps up (fits, keeps up with no margin, or can't keep up). If it doesn't fit, try changes closest first (a smaller program file, a lower quality preset, half the frame rate, one ISO file fewer) and recommend the closest that fits, as a patch for `plan` and `apply`. `start` warns when a setup exceeds what this measured. Runs in isocastd

Usage: isocast tune [OPTIONS] [SETUP]

Arguments:
  [SETUP]  

Options:
      --folder <FOLDER>  Benchmark writing to this folder instead of recording.folder
      --json             
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## isocast capacity

```text
Predict, instantly and without benchmarking, whether a setup's files (the live setup's, at its sources' live formats, if none is given) fit this Mac's video encoders, from measured per-chip data, and list the closest changes that fit as patches for `plan` and `apply`. `tune` measures instead. Runs in isocastd

Usage: isocast capacity [OPTIONS] [SETUP]

Arguments:
  [SETUP]  

Options:
      --stream            Count the stream's encode (default: the live setup's if it streams now; a given setup's if it has a stream)
      --no-stream         Leave the stream's encode out
      --add-iso <SOURCE>  How to turn on this source's ISO file so the setup still fits
      --json              
  -h, --help              Print help
```

## isocast optimize

```text
Optimize the live setup for recording, streaming or both, like OBS's Auto-Configuration Wizard: recording favours quality and ISO files; streaming sets the service and a bitrate from the upload speed (tested unless --upload-kbps is given; a custom server only with `isocast stream speed-test`). Then `tune` benchmarks this Mac and steps down where it can't keep up. Prints a one-line summary and the changes; --apply makes them. Runs in isocastd

Usage: isocast optimize [OPTIONS] <GOAL>

Arguments:
  <GOAL>  recording, streaming or both

Options:
      --service <SERVICE>          Streaming: custom, twitch, youtube, kick or facebook; the live setup's if absent
      --server <SERVER>            Streaming: the ingest server, rtmp://host/app or rtmps://…
      --upload-kbps <UPLOAD_KBPS>  Streaming: the upload speed in kb/s, instead of testing it
      --folder <FOLDER>            Benchmark writing to this folder instead of recording.folder
      --apply                      Make the changes
      --json                       
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

## isocast stream

```text
Stream the program live over RTMP or RTMPS to the live setup's [stream] service, and keep its stream key in the Keychain

Usage: isocast stream <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start       Go live: stream the program (the canvas and the program mix) to the live setup's [stream] service, starting the live engine if needed. Recordings start and stop without touching it. Returns once live, or says why not
  stop        Stop streaming
  status      Show the stream's state, bitrates, dropped frames, congestion and reconnects, and whether a stream key is set
  key         Keep or remove the stream key (in the Keychain, never in a setup)
  speed-test  Measure the upload speed to the service's ingest (a short publish of filler: Twitch's bandwidth test mode, or a custom server, which shows it for a few seconds if it relays to a live service) and recommend a stream bitrate. YouTube, Facebook and Kick have no test mode, so they get a safe bitrate instead, with the reason
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast replay

```text
The replay buffer: keep the last seconds of the program in memory, and save them to a file on demand

Usage: isocast replay <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start   Start keeping the last `recording.replay.seconds` of the program (video and the program mix) in memory, starting the live engine if needed. Recording and streaming start and stop without touching it
  stop    Stop the replay buffer, discarding what it holds
  save    Save what the buffer holds, up to now, to a new file in the recordings folder (the running recording's project folder, if one records). Prints the file's path
  status  Show whether it runs, what it holds, its memory, losses and last save
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast debug

```text
Developer mode, for testing a build locally: verbose logs of every API call and component, and frame timing traces while recording

Usage: isocast debug <COMMAND>

Commands:
  on      Turn developer mode on in the current profile: every API call and debug messages logged, and frame timing traced each second while recording, in their own log segments (`isocast logs`). It turns itself off after 24 hours unless --auto-off-hours says otherwise
  off     Turn developer mode off
  status  Whether developer mode is on, until when, its logs and the latest trace
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## isocast watch

```text
Print events from isocastd as they happen, until Ctrl-C

Usage: isocast watch [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --levels          Also show audio levels (about 20 a second while the live engine runs); isocastd doesn't send them otherwise
      --kinds <KINDS>   Only these kinds of events, like `scene_changed,stopped` (setup_changed, started, status, warning, scene_changed, preview_changed, marker, stream, stopped, levels, source_changed, engine_changed, library_changed, plugin_changed, data_changed, timeline_changed, export_progress, export_finished)
      --except <KINDS>  Leave out these kinds of events, like `status,source_changed`
      --json            
  -h, --help            Print help
```

## isocast frame

```text
Save the live engine's newest frame of the program (the default), studio mode's preview, or a video source as a JPEG. Starts the engine if it isn't running

Usage: isocast frame [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  `program`, `preview` or a source id [default: program]

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  Where to save it; `<target>.jpg` if absent
      --width <WIDTH>    Scale it down to at most this many pixels wide
      --json             
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## isocast frames

```text
Record what a monitor shows: the live engine's low-latency H.264 stream of the program (the default), studio mode's preview or a video source, saved as an H.264 elementary stream (Annex B, which ffprobe and ffplay read). Starts the engine if it isn't running

Usage: isocast frames [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]  `program`, `preview` or a source id [default: program]

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>    Where to save it; `<target>.h264` if absent
      --width <WIDTH>      Scale it down to at most this many pixels wide
      --height <HEIGHT>    With --shared, scale it down to at most this many pixels high
      --fps <FPS>          The most frames a second (30 if absent, at most 60)
      --seconds <SECONDS>  Stop after this long (5 s if absent) [default: 5]
      --shared             Watch through GPU surfaces shared with the daemon (zero-copy, as the native app does) instead of saving H.264: reports the rate, how late frames arrive and the setup revisions they show
      --slots <SLOTS>      With --shared: surfaces in the ring (4 if absent, 2 to 8)
      --filtered           With --shared and a source: through the source's filters, as the program shows it
      --check              With --shared: read every frame back through this process's GPU and fail on black frames or pixels the daemon never drew
      --expect <EXPECT>    With --check: a pixel some frame must have, as X,Y=#RRGGBB (X and Y fractions of the width and height). Repeatable
      --touch              With --check: halfway through, apply an empty live change (the setup stays the same, its revision goes up) and check frames show the new revision
      --json               
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## isocast engine

```text
Keep the live engine running (`start`), or let it stop once nothing needs it (`stop`). It runs the live setup's sources, program and mix all the time, so recording starts at once; it also runs while recording or while a client shows frames

  start  Start the live engine and keep it running
  stop   Let the live engine stop once nothing needs it
```
